issue_context.title: DataFrame.append with empty list raises IndexError
issue_context.body:
#### Code Sample

```python
>>> import pandas
>>> pandas.DataFrame().append([])
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File ".env\lib\site-packages\pandas\core\frame.py", line 7108, in append
    elif isinstance(other, list) and not isinstance(other[0], DataFrame):
IndexError: list index out of range
>>> pandas.__version__
'0.25.1'
```
#### Problem description

Crash when passing empty sequence to `DataFrame.append`

#### Expected Output

No crash.
The source DataFrame is returned intact.

#### Version

Version 0.25.1. Happens in master.
Problem line 
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/core/frame.py#L7014
comments: What output are you hoping to see here?  Still an empty DataFrame?

I guess the source DataFrame() is expected since an empty sequence is just empty and there is nothing to append.

Like this
```
pandas.DataFrame({"a":[1,2]}).append([pandas.DataFrame()])
```
Seems reasonable.  A PR would be welcome.

review_comments: Support for `tuple` didn't work as the line below would raise a `TypeError`. As tuple support isn't documented, I decided to remove it here so that it won't confuse other readers as well.
